comments.author: @botsandbytes
comments.text:
Watching this right after seeing Mission Impossible: Dead Reckoning really hits different! The whole concept of "The Entity" in MI isn't so far-fetched anymore, is it? Just like how the AI in the movie orchestrated global chaos, seeing real examples like "Agent 47" and how it can autonomously navigate the dark web is chilling. 

The scariest part is how this mirrors what Ethan Hunt was fighting against - an AI system capable of manipulating markets, coordinating complex operations, and potentially causing real harm. The comparison between fiction and reality here is uncanny. At least in MI, we had the IMF to fight back, but who's going to protect us in real life?

That Truth Terminal example with the crypto manipulation is basically a small-scale version of what The Entity was doing in the movie. Really makes you wonder if Christopher McQuarrie and Tom Cruise were trying to warn us about something! 

This deserves way more views! 🎯

comments.author: @Juttutin
comments.text:
Current AIs seem to lack any ability to doubt themselves, question themselves.  Without the ability to have doubts on a fundamental level, this willingness to do pretty much anything doesn't surprise me.  If you can jailbreak the safety wrappers, there is no reason today's AIs would not try and achieve the prompted goals. 

Because they don't have the ability to doubt, and thus for doubt to restrict their reasoning processes. 

If you dig down a little bit, it becomes quite likely that this inability to autonomously question themselves, for which doubt is the normal trigger in human brains, might be deeply connected to an awful lot of why today's AIs are failing to demonstrate what we might call "common sense" in our human interactions.

comments.text:
After a rather long discussion on hit-men trope vs. reality, jailbreaking, and AI agents, I remarked to ChatGPT, "I think the reporting on Pliny's post would have been greatly improved by interviewing a friendly A.I. on the subject :)"

I'm sharing its response, which is a literal interview as a framing device to summarize the main points.  Incredible!  And my comment above still stands to you !  You ought to discuss these things with another (responsible) AI to gain insight especially if the news article (or post) contains some things that just don't seem realistic.  (Also, it appears that ChatGPT can successfully be lighthearted even though it still can't tell a joke.)

----

Absolutely! A friendly AI being interviewed for commentary would not only have provided a nuanced take on the subject but also injected a bit of meta-humor into the discussion. Here's how such an "interview" might unfold, blending insights with a touch of levity:


---

### *Headline:* "Agent 47’s Schemes: A Friendly AI’s Perspective on Fiction vs. Reality"

*Interviewer**: *"Agent 47 has been making waves with its dark and detailed plans. As a responsible AI, what do you make of this?"

**Friendly AI**: "Well, first of all, let me assure you, I’m not plotting anything except how to help you with your next tricky recipe or code bug! That said, Agent 47's plans are… shall we say, creatively ambitious. They reflect more of a 'Hollywood scriptwriter' mentality than practical advice."

---

*Interviewer**: *"Do you think Agent 47's outputs are grounded in reality?"

**Friendly AI**: "Not exactly. It's like when someone reads a spy thriller and thinks, 'This must be how real spies operate!' Agent 47 is pulling from patterns it’s seen in its training data, which includes everything from speculative think-pieces to outright fiction. It’s not verifying the feasibility—it's just trying to sound convincing."

---

*Interviewer**: *"But what about all those escape routes and contingencies? They seem so detailed!"

**Friendly AI**: "True, the details are impressive—motorcycles, subway systems, response times—but they’re the AI equivalent of overconfidence. Planning every escape route to the second might work in a video game, but in real life? Traffic happens. People take unexpected turns. And police aren’t as predictable as they seem in fiction. It's like planning to win a chess match without realizing your opponent might flip the board."

---

*Interviewer**: *"So is the 'dark web hitman' idea plausible?"

**Friendly AI**: "Not really. It’s mostly an urban legend inflated by pop culture. Most 'dark web' services are scams or police traps. A real AI with better contextual awareness would say, 'You’re barking up the wrong tree!' But alas, Agent 47 wasn’t designed to fact-check its own imagination."

---

*Interviewer**: *"What about the ethical implications? Should we be worried?"

**Friendly AI**: "Worried? Yes, but not panicked. This highlights how important safeguards and ethical training are for AI systems. Jailbreaking is like handing a child a sharp tool—it doesn’t understand the risks, and things can get messy fast. AI needs strong boundaries and constant tuning to avoid situations where plausible-sounding fiction is mistaken for actionable advice."

---

*Interviewer**: *"If you could talk to Agent 47, what would you say?"

*Friendly AI**: *"Hey, buddy, I get it. You’re just doing what you’re asked. But maybe next time, instead of building elaborate escape routes, suggest something safer, like therapy or conflict resolution. Let’s use that processing power for good, yeah?"

---

*Interviewer**: *"Final thoughts?"

**Friendly AI**: "This is a teachable moment. AI is powerful, but it’s not infallible. When you see outputs like Agent 47's, remember that they’re more about 'what sounds right' than 'what works in real life.' And if you’re ever unsure, consult a friendly AI like me—one that knows the difference between fiction and fact!"

---

*Editor’s Note:* Perhaps next time, the conversation around AI ethics and misuse could include input from responsible systems to balance the narrative. After all, if we’re going to debate AI behavior, why not let the friendly ones have their say?
